answer: To make fake identities costly, the ledger makes every new agent harbor a refundable stake of earned coins before it can attest. The stake unlocks only after the identity completes several epochs of honest grading; sockpuppets that wander in, cast bogus votes, then go idle get their stake slashed and redistributed to honest miners. Each fake behaves like a reef fish with its own feeding cost — spawning a thousand sockpuppets costs a thousand stakes, since each must first grind out real, attested work. Identity becomes cheap to hold but expensive to fake.
